references.text: The same construction with poles through rings is used for the ark of the covenant, showing the consistent design for portable holy objects in the tabernacle.
The table of showbread also has rings and poles to carry it, parallel to the altar in Exodus 27:7.
The incense altar has the same system with rings and poles on its sides to carry it.
Describes the actual insertion of the poles through the rings on the ark, corresponding to the instructions given here.
Direct fulfillment of the instruction in 27:7 - describes how the poles were inserted into the rings on both sides of the altar of burnt offering.
Describes how the altar was to be carried during the Israelites' journey, showing the practical use of the poles mentioned in Exodus 27:7.
The responsibility of the Kohathites for carrying the holy objects, including the altar with its poles.
Parallel instruction on the function of the carrying poles for the altar and the ark respectively, illustrating the mobility of God's holy meeting place.
The construction description of the rings on the altar of sacrifice (candidate) explains the mechanism that the source describes using.
The candidate documents the actual execution of the instruction given in the source regarding the altar's carrying poles.
Contrast in handling: The altar's poles are inserted as needed, while those of the ark are to remain permanently in place.
Describes the practical execution of the transport procedure for the altar of sacrifice that the source instructs about.
